news.headline: Findings from our driver behavior study in Colorado
A playbook from our partnership with Prince George’s County to improve traffic safety

paragraphs: Obvio sells automated traffic safety cameras to towns and cities. The company describes context-aware technology that helps cities track reckless behavior, educate drivers and enforce traffic laws. School zone violations are among the behaviors the cameras target.

Installation is described as taking about a week, with no power or utility permissions needed. The hardware is said to hold up through winter storms and snow. Processing happens on the device, which the company says lets a single camera detect a wide variety of reckless behavior. Alongside enforcement, the site lists community dashboards and yard signs. Warning letters carry video proof of what happened. Real-time detection is presented as a way to increase transparency and awareness.

Testimonials come from police chiefs and town officials in Maryland, including the chief in the Town of Colmar Manor. The company states that it is funded by venture capital firms. A banner on the site points to a Virginia stop sign and crosswalk enforcement law taking effect July 1, 2026.

quote.text: Our mission is to curb reckless driving and save lives on our roadways
